newsitem.title: USA: Investigators probe Florida skydiving tragedy.
newsitem.headline: Investigators probe Florida skydiving tragedy.

text.p: Investigators on Monday examined the wreckage of a small plane to determine why it crashed into a Florida potato field, killing the pilot and five members of a skydiving team.
The sole survivor of Sunday's disaster, a woman who parachuted from the plane as it went into a spin, was "extremely distraught" and requested privacy, police said.

Jeff Kennedy, an investigator for the National Transportation Safety Board, said overloading did not appear to be the cause of the crash, as was initially thought. But he said the problem could have been uneven weight distribution of the passengers and their equipment.

The Cessna model 210-5, ran into trouble shortly after takeoff from Homestead Airport, just south of Miami, on Sunday afternoon. As horrified picnickers watched, it spun to the ground, belly flopped and burst in to flames.
Killed instantly were the pilot, the owner of Homestead-based Skydivers Inc. and four other skydivers.

The survivor, Carol 0'Connell, 43, told police she stepped onto the plane's strut ready to jump when she saw the pilot having difficulty controlling the plane. As it began to spin, she decided to jump. The plane hit the ground before she did.
She told reporters at her home late on Sunday: "I can't explain why I'm still alive while these others left behind many loved ones. I guess when it's your time to go, you go. It wasn't my time."
Police issued a statement on Monday saying O'Connell was too upset to grant any more interviews.
